headline: Crop Yield Shocks and Nutritional Collapse
summary: Every fraction of a degree increases the likelihood of simultaneous harvest failures across major breadbaskets, triggering food price spikes that hit the poorest hardest.
sourceName: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch 5 & Zhao et al. (PNAS)
statLabel: Maize yield loss per 1°C of warming without adaptation
socialImplication: Families in low-income nations spend 40% to 60% of their total income on food (versus ~10% in high-income nations). A 20% spike in grain prices forces households to skip meals or pull children from school.

headline: Glacial Depletion and Deepening Aquifer Strain
summary: Hydrological extremes compress clean water into shorter, violent deluge cycles while lengthening dry seasons, leaving billions with insecure municipal access.
sourceName: IPCC AR6 WGII Ch 4 & UN Water
statLabel: Projected people in chronic water stress at 2°C
socialImplication: When piped water fails, water-fetching labor falls overwhelmingly on women and girls—costing up to 200 million collective hours every day globally and increasing vulnerability to gender-based violence.

headline: Lethal Wet-Bulb Temperatures & Lost Work Hours
summary: The physiological ceiling of human labor is already being tested in tropical and subtropical regions. Beyond 35°C wet-bulb, the body cannot cool itself via evaporation.
sourceName: ILO (2019) & WHO Climate and Health Report
statLabel: Full-time equivalent jobs lost annually to heat stress by 2030
unit: Percentage of Working Hours Lost by 2030
socialImplication: Informal and outdoor workers face an agonizing trade-off between heatstroke or starvation. Many endure chronic kidney disease of non-traditional origin (CKDnt) from repetitive heat-stress dehydration.

headline: Inhabitable Coastlines & Weather-Driven Migration
summary: Extreme cyclones, storm surges, and riverine flooding tear through informal urban settlements and rural river basins, generating millions of internal refugees annually.
sourceName: IDMC Global Report on Internal Displacement (GRID 2023)
socialImplication: Most climate migrants move within their national borders to crowded peri-urban informal settlements with precarious tenure, where they remain vulnerable to the next severe storm.
